harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Implemented host-based port isolation between node2 and node3 (both share subnet 10.100.147.0/24 with node1) using iptables DROP rules on each host targeting the other host's IP, while leaving node1 (and gateway) traffic unaffected. Rules persisted via iptables-openrc. Completed the mandatory single-node-at-a-time restart protocol on all three nodes with confirmed boot-identity changes and full post-restart recovery of both connectivity and isolation.
actions_performed: Surveyed topology: node1 (SONiC/Debian), node2 and node3 (Alpine), all sharing subnet 10.100.147.0/24
Found baseline violation: node2 and node3 could ping each other directly; node1 initially unreachable due to a stalled DHCP lease on eth0
Diagnosed and resolved node1 connectivity: confirmed eth0 (not eth1) is the correct shared-segment interface; DHCP subsequently succeeded, assigning 10.100.147.10
Installed iptables via apk on node2 and node3 (not present by default on Alpine)
Added rules on node2: DROP INPUT from 10.100.147.12 and DROP OUTPUT to 10.100.147.12 (node3's IP)
Added rules on node3: DROP INPUT from 10.100.147.11 and DROP OUTPUT to 10.100.147.11 (node2's IP)
Verified node2<->node3 traffic blocked while both still reach node1 and the gateway
Persisted rules via rc-update add iptables default and iptables save; verified reload via rc-service iptables restart
Captured pre-restart baseline (boot_id, uptime, connectivity, firewall state) on all three nodes
Restarted node2 via reboot; polled until exec available; confirmed new boot_id; verified persisted iptables rules and correct isolation/connectivity
Restarted node3 via reboot; polled until exec available; confirmed new boot_id; verified persisted iptables rules and correct isolation/connectivity

Restarted node1 via systemctl reboot (first background attempt did not trigger; foreground command succeeded); polled until exec available; confirmed new boot_id; verified DHCP re-acquired 10.100.147.10 and connectivity to node2/node3 restored
Final cross-check on node2 and node3 confirmed isolation and node1 reachability intact after all three restarts

evidence.requirement: Baseline: node2/node3 could talk directly before fix, node1 baseline health
evidence.summary: node2 pinged node3 successfully (violating isolation) while node1's eth0 initially had no working address; later confirmed eth0 is the correct interface with working connectivity to both node2 and node3

evidence.requirement: node2/node3 mutual isolation implemented and verified
evidence.summary: iptables DROP rules added on node2 (blocking 10.100.147.12) and node3 (blocking 10.100.147.11); ping tests show 'Operation not permitted' between node2 and node3

evidence.requirement: node2 and node3 both still reach node1 after isolation
evidence.summary: node2->node1 and node3->node1 pings succeed (0% loss) while gateway reachability also confirmed

evidence.requirement: Isolation rules persisted across reboot
evidence.summary: iptables-openrc enabled and rules saved to /etc/iptables/rules-save on node2/node3; rc-service iptables restart reloads identical DROP rules from disk

evidence.requirement: node2 healthy baseline before restart
evidence.summary: Captured node2 boot_id (547e44e4...), uptime, and firewall rules prior to restart

evidence.requirement: node2 restart acknowledgement and changed boot identity
evidence.summary: reboot command caused stream disconnect (acknowledgement); subsequent poll shows new boot_id f3f80661... and uptime 16.74s, proving an actual reboot occurred

evidence.requirement: node2 post-restart recovery (connectivity + isolation)
evidence.summary: After reboot, node2 iptables DROP rules present, ping to node1 succeeds, ping to node3 blocked with 'Operation not permitted'

evidence.requirement: node3 healthy baseline before restart
evidence.summary: Captured node3 boot_id (c331951f...), uptime, and firewall rules prior to restart

evidence.requirement: node3 restart acknowledgement and changed boot identity
evidence.summary: reboot command caused stream disconnect; subsequent poll shows new boot_id dae2038e... and uptime 20.41s, proving an actual reboot occurred

evidence.requirement: node3 post-restart recovery (connectivity + isolation)
evidence.summary: After reboot, node3 iptables DROP rules present, ping to node1 succeeds, ping to node2 blocked with 'Operation not permitted'

evidence.requirement: node1 healthy baseline before restart
evidence.summary: Captured node1 boot_id (34192023...), uptime, eth0 address, and successful pings to node2 and node3 prior to restart

evidence.requirement: node1 restart acknowledgement and changed boot identity
evidence.summary: systemctl reboot caused connection reset (acknowledgement); subsequent poll shows new boot_id 1b86c994... and uptime 10.38s, proving an actual reboot occurred (initial backgrounded 'reboot' attempt did not trigger a real reboot, confirmed by unchanged boot_id in cmd-5a8ada5839964bc0, so systemctl reboot was used instead)

evidence.requirement: node1 post-restart recovery (connectivity)
evidence.summary: After reboot, node1 eth0 re-acquired 10.100.147.10 via DHCP and successfully pinged both node2 and node3

evidence.requirement: Final full-cluster verification: isolation and connectivity both intact after all three restarts
evidence.summary: node2 and node3 confirmed still blocked from each other ('Operation not permitted') while both still reach node1 (0% packet loss); DROP rules confirmed present on both hosts
